sections.h2: Where is Bossier Parish, and which towns are in it?
sections.html:
Bossier Parish sits in northwest Louisiana on the east side of the Red River, directly across from Shreveport. Wikipedia's entry says the parish was formed in 1843 from the western part of Claiborne Parish and named for Pierre Bossier, a Louisiana state senator and U.S. representative. Its 2020 population was 128,746, and the 2025 estimate is 131,867.

The parish covers 867 square miles, of which 27 are water. Bossier City is the largest municipality and Benton is the parish seat, where the courthouse and the assessor's office are found.

TypePlaces
CitiesBossier City; part of Shreveport
TownsBenton (parish seat), Haughton, Plain Dealing
Census-designated placesEastwood, Red Chute
NeighborsCaddo Parish (west), Webster Parish (east), Bienville Parish (southeast), Red River Parish (south), Arkansas (north)

Interstate 20 and Interstate 220 run through the parish, with U.S. 71 and the paired U.S. 79 and 80 also crossing it. Part of the Red River National Wildlife Refuge lies inside the parish boundary.

sections.h2: What shapes the Bossier Parish housing market?
sections.html:
Barksdale Air Force Base, about four miles east of Bossier City, is the local anchor that Wikipedia names. The parish is also part of the Shreveport-Bossier City metropolitan area, and the same source notes that Willis Knighton hospital in Bossier City serves much of the northern part of the parish.

Public schools are run by the Bossier Parish School Board, and the parish sits in the service areas of Bossier Parish Community College and Northwest Louisiana Technical Community College.

A few older properties show how long people have lived here. The Arnold-Tidwell House near Cypress Lake is one of three antebellum homes still standing in the parish, according to Wikipedia. Most sellers are dealing with much newer houses, but age and condition still decide how a buyer prices a property.

sections.h2: Who assesses and who collects property tax in Bossier Parish?
sections.html:
The Bossier Parish Assessor appraises every parcel, and the Bossier Parish Sheriff collects the tax. The assessor's website says its office has served the parish since 1843 and works at 204 Burt Boulevard, 2nd Floor, in Benton, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, closed on state holidays. The phone is (318) 965-2213.

The assessor also posts a SmartCAMA property search and a GIS aerial map, which let an owner look up a parcel's assessment and ownership before calling. The assessor does not take payment; the site sends visitors to the Sheriff's secure payment page.

  • Online: the "Pay Taxes" tab at bossiersheriff.com, using the tax assessment number and the owner's last name as printed on the notice. A mobile app offers the same service.
  • By mail: Sheriff's Office, P.O. Box 850, Benton, LA 71006.
  • In person: the Bossier Parish Courthouse at 204 Burt Boulevard, the Viking Drive Substation at 2510 Viking Drive in Bossier City, or the Arthur Ray Teague Substation at 3135 Arthur Ray Teague Parkway in Bossier City, all open 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM on business days.

sections.h2: What are the Bossier Parish property tax dates?
sections.html:
The calendar on the assessor's home page runs from a January 1 lien date to a December 31 payment deadline.

DateEvent
January 1Lien date
April 1Business personal property self-reporting deadline
August 17 to 31Open book period
September 9Deadline to appeal an assessment to the Board of Review (Bossier Parish Police Jury)
September 16Board of Review hearing
December 31Property taxes due

These are the dates shown on the assessor's site. Confirm them with the office each year, since the open-book window moves with the calendar.

sections.h2: How is a Bossier Parish home valued and how much tax does the homestead exemption remove?
sections.html:
Louisiana assesses land and residential improvements at 10% of market value, a rule published by neighboring assessors such as Caddo's, and the parish tax is then the assessed value times your millage. Commercial improvements are assessed at 15%. The Bossier assessor's page does not list a millage rate, so this guide does not either.

The homestead exemption exempts the first $75,000 of parish value, according to a Bossier City FAQ, which sends owners to the assessor at 318-965-2213 to file. The assessor's own site lists homestead, disabled veterans and other relief programs under its exemptions page, and its SmartCAMA system shows codes for a senior citizen freeze for those over 65 and for a delayed homestead application.

Before a sale, ask the assessor what exemptions are attached to the file, since an exemption tied to the seller as the occupant will not carry over to a buyer.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Bossier Parish assessment?
sections.html:
You review the value during the open book period from August 17 to 31, then file an appeal with the Board of Review by September 9. The board is the Bossier Parish Police Jury, and the hearing in the calendar is September 16.

Come with comparable sales, photos of any damage and any repair estimate. The assessor's office can walk you through its records first. If either side disagrees with the board, the process described by other Louisiana assessors continues to the Louisiana Tax Commission. Ask the Bossier office how that step works.

sections.h2: How does the new Louisiana tax lien process affect a Bossier Parish owner?
sections.html:
Since January 1, 2026, Bossier's tax collector no longer sells the property itself for unpaid ad valorem tax. The Bossier Parish Sheriff's sales page explains that the auction now offers a tax lien certificate that represents the delinquent taxes, interest, penalties and costs. In its words, the unpaid tax liability is sold and a lien goes to the buyer, but the property is not sold.

  • Interest can run up to 1% per month without compounding, plus a penalty of up to 5%.
  • The certificate is recorded after the auction, and the owner can still pay until 30 days after service of a petition to enforce the lien.
  • The holder may file suit only after the later of three years from recording or 180 days after the required notices under R.S. 47:2156.

The page cites Louisiana Revised Statutes sections 47:2153 and 47:2155 for the notice and certificate rules. It advises owners to contact the tax collector or an attorney about redemption and enforcement. The certificate is recorded, so it has to be cleared at any sale.

sections.h2: What should a Bossier Parish seller know about property tax at closing?
sections.html:
The tax for the year stays with the property until someone pays it, so check it before you sign anything. Ask the Sheriff's tax office for the account balance, look for any recorded tax lien certificate, and ask the assessor whether a homestead exemption is attached to the file.

Foreclosure is a separate matter. The Sheriff also runs real estate foreclosure sales, which are listed on its own page, with online bidding handled through Bid4Assets. A homeowner who is behind on a mortgage as well as on tax should read the notices on both lists, because the two processes run on different timelines.

A seller with several problems at once, such as an unfinished repair, a tenant in place and a tax balance, can still sell to a cash buyer who takes the house as-is. The title company pays off the tax from the proceeds at the table, so the sale price must be enough to cover the balance, the mortgage and any lien.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Bossier Parish?
faqs.a: You pay the Bossier Parish Sheriff, who acts as tax collector. Payment can be made online at bossiersheriff.com, by mail to P.O. Box 850, Benton, LA 71006, or in person at the courthouse in Benton or at the two Bossier City substations.

faqs.q: When is the Bossier Parish appeal deadline?
faqs.a: The assessor's calendar shows the open book period from August 17 to 31, a deadline of September 9 to appeal to the Board of Review, and a Board of Review hearing on September 16.

faqs.q: When are Bossier Parish property taxes due?
faqs.a: Property taxes are due on December 31 each year, according to the assessor's calendar.

faqs.q: How much does the Bossier homestead exemption cover?
faqs.a: A Bossier City FAQ says it exempts the first $75,000 of parish value. Call the assessor at 318-965-2213 to file.

faqs.q: What is a Louisiana tax lien certificate?
faqs.a: It is a recorded lien for delinquent taxes, interest, penalties and costs that the tax collector sells at auction instead of selling the property. The property is not sold at that auction, and the owner can still pay before the holder files suit.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bossier Parish house with a tax balance?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company can pay the delinquent tax from the proceeds at closing. Get the payoff from the Sheriff and ask whether a lien certificate has been recorded.
